# Git Workflow Strategy

The assignment is divided into separate Quarto documents so that each group member can work independently on their own branch without interfering with the work of the others.

At the beginning of the project, one group member created the GitHub repository and prepared the overall Quarto structure, including the main document, section files, headings, and folder organization. This made the group work more structured and efficient from the start.

Each student then worked on their assigned section in a separate branch. Once a section was completed, checked, and reviewed, the branch was merged into `main`. The master Quarto document combines all sections into the final report.

| Student | Assigned Sections | Main Tasks |
|---|---|---|
| Jennifer Houmard | `02_data_preparation.qmd` and `04_regression_and_figure.qmd` | Data cleaning and reorganization, preparation of the final dataset, linear regression analysis, publication figure, and figure interpretation |
| Valentin Balbine | `03_anova_analysis.qmd` | Mixed-design ANOVA, interpretation of the main effects and `GROUP × ID` interaction, and interaction visualization |
| Shakir Nasir | `01_think_before_coding.qmd` and `05_discussion.qmd` | Scientific question, analysis strategy, required libraries, comparison with the original article, and final discussion |

The group also discussed and brainstormed the **Challenges and Lessons Learned** section together so that it reflects the main difficulties encountered during the assignment and the solutions developed as a group.

# Challenges and Lessons Learned

One challenge was cleaning the original dataset before performing the statistical analysis. We had to check whether all groups had completed the same ID conditions and repetitions. We found that `ID3` was incomplete for the stroke group and that `R3` was not completed consistently across all groups. We therefore had to decide how to reorganize the data so that the comparisons between groups were based on the same conditions.

We also had to distinguish between the different levels of data used in the analysis. The ANOVA and regression required participant-level mean Movement Time values, while the publication figure used the cleaned trial-level data to calculate the mean and standard deviation for each `GROUP × ID` combination. Understanding why different summarized datasets were needed was initially confusing but helped us better understand how the structure of the data depends on the purpose of the analysis.

Creating the final publication figure was also challenging. We had to make sure that the means, standard deviations, regression lines, and error bars were calculated from the correct dataset. This required checking the data structure carefully and understanding why using participant-level data or trial-level data produced different error bars.

Overall, these challenges helped us improve our understanding of data cleaning and manipulation in R, mixed-design ANOVA, regression analysis, effect sizes, statistical interpretation, data visualization, and collaborative work using Git and GitHub.

# Grading Checklist

- [✓] Scientific question clearly focuses on the `GROUP × ID` interaction.
- [✓] Data cleaning is explained, including why `ID3` and `R3` were removed.
- [✓] Mixed-design ANOVA is run correctly and reports F, df, p-values, and `ges`.
- [✓] Significance is interpreted using `α = 0.01`.
- [✓] `GROUP × ID` interaction is correctly explained.
- [✓] Separate regressions are run for `ap`, `cp`, and `pp`, with equations and slope interpretation.
- [✓] Publication figure includes mean values, error bars, regression lines, labels, and equations.
- [✓] Results are compared clearly with Mottet et al. (2017).
- [✓] Limitations are discussed, including the reduced dataset and lack of post-hoc pairwise comparisons.
- [✓] Git workflow and group responsibilities are explained.
- [✓] Challenges and lessons learned are included.
- [✓] Final master Quarto document renders from start to finish without errors.
